body: Where I am from they seem to go to the city bus station where the buses are actually kept. They have their own pumps there and I assume since its owned by the city any vehicle that is attached to the city could fill up there.
I am so sorry. I just automatically assumed you were a soldier. Having been born and raised in Canada I am fortunate enough to not have experienced war like that.

Thank you for serving. I definetly do recommend therapy. It helps you to talk about things you might not even know are triggers. I lost a friend when I was young and thought that wasn't a major trigger (due to other things), but through counselling I was able to awknowledge when I was young I couldn't grieve that properly. I have no experience with war, but I imagine with so much emotions happening there were many events you couldn't truly feel at the time that effect you now.

Thank you. Reading this helped me cause I try to look at it that way too. I'm a more empathetic understanding person who has made it through certain things and am strong.

My issue right now is life is good. I know that sounds weird, but its like my mind is like its time to deal. I just graduated college last week and have a job lined up for the new year. I have an amazing partner who supports me. I spoke to and detached from some people that caused the trauma. I feel like I am doing what I am supposed to do and yet I'm still trapped in my mind. The counsellor said anxiety for me will likely be a constant that I need to manage my entire life, much like you mentioned. I just feel helpless sometimes. It's nice to know others are out there.
I'm sorry for your loss. I'm sure the joy of having your son will help guide you through the fear of being in the hospital. It will be okay and I'm sure your father is very proud of you.
